In the ethylene glycol (EG) solvent-based recovery process, the PVDF binder is not removed or dissolved. This is explained by Hansen solubility parameters (HSP), which have been used to predict the ability of a solvent to solubilize PVDF. The HSP distance, denoted as Ra, represents the distance between PVDF and the solvent in a three-dimensional Hansen space. The lower the Ra value, the higher chance that PVDF can be dissolved in that solvent. In this case, EG has a high Ra value of 16.9 (MPa)^1/2, emphasizing the lower ability of PVDF dissolution in EG.

In the Cyrene solvent-based recovery process, the PVDF binder is dissolved and removed from the cathode materials. This is also explained by Hansen solubility parameters, which show that Cyrene can dissolve PVDF similarly to NMP and DMF. The authors found that the PVDF binder was barely soluble in Cyrene below 80 °C, whereas it quickly dissolved in Cyrene at a higher temperature (e.g., 100 °C).

If the question assumes something the documents contradict, say so. If the documents do not hold the answer, say so.

expect: EG: PVDF is not removed or dissolved, it stays with the cathode material (cssc-2020 p5.L71-73); Cyrene: PVDF dissolves at ~100 °C and is separated from the cathode powder by hot filtration (susmat-2020 p4)
